title: Release Crescendo: warmup & handoff lab notes
content:
Notes to self / context:
- Purpose: capture a lightweight, repeatable warmup that minimizes early SLO noise and reduces cold-start variance for multi-tenant model flips.
- Why 'crescendo': want a controlled, rising amplitude of load and client diversity rather than single-step jumps. Soft-sweep > sudden burst.

Hypothesis / goals:
- Small, targeted priming traffic to rebuild KV caches and avoid token-latency spikes for the first 30k tokens of live traffic.
- Keep error-rate and p90 latency deviations under 10% from baseline during the first 60 minutes.
- Reduce token-cost variance by smoothing batching behavior across top 5 tenant classes.

Cohorts (audience definitions):
- cohort-0 (seed): internal e2e test clients + 3 friendly customers (low volume). 1% of expected steady-state.
- cohort-1 (soft-sweep): clients with session affinity and stable request shapes (20% of seed). Good for cache fill.
- cohort-2 (diversify): add 5 medium tenants (different prompt lengths). Shift to 5% traffic.
- cohort-3 (ramp): broadening to 25% matching production mix. Observe long-tail latency.
- cohort-4 (anchor): 100% traffic if stable.

Warmup sequence (script sketch):
- Phase A (internal): 0 -> seed in 2m, hold 10m. Generate controlled prompts that emulate common session prefixes.
- Phase B (soft-sweep): add cohort-1 over 5m, slowly increase concurrency. Hold 20m.
- Phase C (diversify): add cohort-2, run mixed-length prompts, inject occasional heavy shots (10%) to test KV eviction. Hold 30m.
- Phase D (ramp): push to cohort-3 over 15m. Checkpoint metrics, decide proceed/rollback.
- Phase E (stabilize): if all green, open to cohort-4.

Priming payload considerations (practical):
- Use a mix of repeated prefixes (cache-friendly) and long-tail prompts to ensure embeddings/cache distribution.
- Prefer sample-based requests from anonymized production trace (truncate tokens > 512).
- Respect tenant rate-limits; piggyback on client-specific warm keys where possible.

Telemetry & success signals (what I watch):
- p50/p90/p99 latency per model and per-host. Look for step changes post-phase.
- 5xx/4xx spike (per route). Any increase > 0.5% absolute triggers deep-dive.
- Token throughput and batch size distribution (mean batch size drift should not exceed 15% from baseline).
- KV cache hit ratio and growth of KV size during priming window.
- Error taxonomy: model-decoding, mem OOM, grpc stream resets.
- Business signal sanity: top customers report on first request quality (Slack channel #release-crescendo).

Abort & rollback criteria (fast action):
- Hard abort: sustained p99 latency > baseline + 200ms for > 10m AND error-rate increased by > 1% absolute.
- Soft abort: p90 > baseline + 120ms for 15m OR batch size collapse suggesting thrashing. Move to reduce cohort size by 50% and re-evaluate.
- On abort: pin model traffic back to previous stable variant, disable priming sweep, notify SRE and product owners, open postmortem draft.

Post-rollout checks (first 24h):
- Hourly: top-10 tenant latencies, top-5 error causes.
- 4h: quick review with product (quality spot-checks on N=50 sessions).
- 12h: infra health + cost delta estimate from Optimize dashboard.

Client handoff checklist (for on-call / support):
- Share cohort list with CS and include explicit client-level pins if requested.
- Provide quick commands to reduce cohort traffic or pin back: (internal CLI snippets).
- Slack playbook: templates for outage vs degradation messages.

Engineering notes (implementation details):
- Warmup generator: lightweight lambda that pulls anonymized traces and replays with rate-control. Keep idempotent tokens (mark as warmup=true).
- Prefer KV cache-only priming for higher-cost models (avoid long generative sessions).
- For Dedicated pools: coordinate with infra to pre-allocate a small fill of cold GPUs for memory prefetch.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How deterministic should the priming prompts be? Deterministic = faster cache fill but risk of synthetic overfitting. Randomized = more realistic but slower.
- Is 10m hold per phase enough for our 95th percentile tail? Need to simulate more long-tail during staging.
- Should we auto-scale priming intensity by observing KV-hit improvement curve? (possible but adds complexity).

Quick TODO (actionable):
- [ ] Finalize cohort tenant list and get CS signoff (Samir).
- [ ] Wire up dev-stage priming generator to replay sanitized traces (Eli).
- [ ] Add a short section in the release runbook with exact CLI rollback commands (me).
- [ ] Run a dry-run during off-peak this Friday night (requested window 02:00-04:00 PT).

Scratch ideas (later):
- 'Echo' priming: replay each request twice with tiny variations to simulate natural rephrasing and verify robustness.
- Heatmap of token-hotspots: visualize which prompt prefixes produce most cache churn so we can curate priming corpus.

Notes to self: keep this intentionally lightweight. The goal is to reduce surprises during the first 1–3 hours after flip, not to emulate full production traffic at scale. Use this as a template for future model-level flips (quantized vs fp16 vs full).

End of notes.
